questions.stem: Which of the following lists the taxonomic ranks in the correct order, from the largest group to the smallest?

options.text: Kingdom, class, phylum, order, family, genus, species
Kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species
Species, genus, family, kingdom, order, class, phylum
Phylum, kingdom, order, class, family, species, genus

questions.explanation: The hierarchy runs kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species. Each rank is contained within the one before it, so a kingdom holds several phyla, a phylum holds several classes, and so on down to species.

distractorRationale.a: Class and phylum have been swapped; a phylum contains classes, not the reverse
distractorRationale.c: This is roughly the reverse order, from smallest to largest, with kingdom misplaced
distractorRationale.d: Kingdom is the largest rank and must come first

questions.stem: Which of the following scientific names is written correctly according to the rules of binomial nomenclature?

options.text: homo sapiens
Zea Mays
Escherichia coli
PLASMODIUM FALCIPARUM

questions.explanation: The genus takes an initial capital and the species is entirely in lower case, so Escherichia coli is correct. In print the name is italicised and in handwriting it is underlined.

distractorRationale.a: The genus name homo must begin with a capital H
distractorRationale.b: The species name mays must not be capitalised
distractorRationale.d: Names are not written in full capitals; only the genus takes a capital letter

questions.stem: An organism is multicellular, has no chlorophyll, has a body made of hyphae with walls containing chitin, and feeds on dead organic matter. To which kingdom does it belong?

options.text: Plantae
Animalia
Fungi
Monera

questions.explanation: Hyphae with chitin walls and the absence of chlorophyll are the diagnostic features of the kingdom Fungi, and feeding on dead organic matter is saprophytic nutrition, which is typical of fungi such as Rhizopus and mushrooms.

distractorRationale.a: Plants have chlorophyll and cellulose walls, and no hyphae
distractorRationale.b: Animals have no cell wall at all
distractorRationale.d: Monera are prokaryotic and unicellular, so they cannot have a multicellular body of hyphae

questions.stem: Two organisms belong to the same family but to different genera. Which statement about them is correct?

options.text: They must belong to the same species
They belong to the same order and the same class
They belong to different kingdoms
They can interbreed to produce fertile offspring

questions.explanation: Because the hierarchy is nested, sharing a family automatically means sharing every rank above it — order, class, phylum and kingdom. They differ only from genus downwards.

distractorRationale.a: Species is below genus, so organisms in different genera cannot share a species
distractorRationale.c: Sharing a family means they must share the same kingdom
distractorRationale.d: Only members of the same species interbreed to give fertile offspring

questions.stem: Amoeba, Paramecium and Plasmodium are all placed in the kingdom Protista because they are

options.text: prokaryotic and lack a nucleus
eukaryotic but simple in organisation, without true tissues
multicellular with cellulose cell walls
all parasites of humans

questions.explanation: Protists have a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles, so they are eukaryotes, but their bodies are unicellular or simple colonies with no differentiated tissues or organs. That combination is what separates them from Monera on one side and from plants, animals and fungi on the other.

distractorRationale.a: All three have a true nucleus, which makes them eukaryotic, not prokaryotic
distractorRationale.c: They are unicellular and do not have cellulose walls
distractorRationale.d: Amoeba and Paramecium are free-living; only Plasmodium is a parasite

questions.stem: A horse and a donkey can mate and produce a mule, but the mule is sterile. What does this show?

options.text: The horse and the donkey belong to the same species
The horse and the donkey are different species
The mule is a new species
The horse and the donkey belong to different families

questions.explanation: The test for a species is the production of *fertile* offspring. The mule cannot reproduce, so the two parents fail the test and are separate species — both are in the genus Equus but they are Equus caballus and Equus asinus.

distractorRationale.a: Same-species matings give fertile offspring, which this mating does not
distractorRationale.c: A sterile hybrid cannot form a breeding population, so it is not a species
distractorRationale.d: They are close enough to mate at all, which shows the same genus, let alone the same family

questions.stem: Why do biologists use scientific names instead of local or common names?

options.text: Scientific names are shorter than common names
One species may have many different local names, but only one scientific name, which is used worldwide
Local names cannot be written down
Scientific names describe the habitat of the organism

questions.explanation: Common names vary between languages and even between villages, and the same name may be applied to different plants in different places. A binomial name is unique and internationally recognised, so scientists reading in any language know exactly which organism is meant.

distractorRationale.a: Scientific names are usually longer, not shorter
distractorRationale.c: Local names are written down all the time; that is not the problem
distractorRationale.d: Some names hint at appearance or place, but naming does not describe habitat as a rule

questions.stem: Bacteria are placed in the kingdom Monera because they have no true nucleus.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: True. Monera are prokaryotes: their DNA is a single circular molecule lying free in the cytoplasm with no nuclear membrane around it, and they also lack mitochondria and other membrane-bound organelles.

questions.stem: As you move down the taxonomic hierarchy from kingdom to species, what happens to the number of organisms in a group and to the number of features they share?

options.text: Both the number of organisms and the number of shared features increase
The number of organisms decreases while the number of shared features increases
The number of organisms increases while the number of shared features decreases
Both remain unchanged

questions.explanation: Each step down applies an extra requirement, so fewer organisms qualify but those that do resemble each other more closely. A kingdom such as Animalia contains millions of very different organisms; a species contains organisms so alike that they interbreed.

distractorRationale.a: Numbers cannot rise as the groups get narrower
distractorRationale.c: This reverses the relationship; narrower groups are more, not less, similar
distractorRationale.d: The whole purpose of the hierarchy is that these quantities change with rank

questions.stem: State the seven taxonomic ranks in order and outline three rules for writing the scientific name of an organism, using one named example.
markingGuide: Ranks in correct order: kingdom, phylum (or division), class, order, family, genus, species (3 marks for the complete correct sequence)
Rule 1: the name has two parts — the genus followed by the species (1 mark)
Rule 2: the genus begins with a capital letter and the species with a small letter (2 marks)
Rule 3: the whole name is italicised in print or underlined in handwriting (1 mark)
Correct worked example given, for example Zea mays or Homo sapiens, written in the correct form (1 mark)
questions.explanation: The ranks must be given in the nested order kingdom down to species. The three marking rules are the two-part structure, the capitalisation convention and the italics or underlining convention, and the example must itself obey all three.
